title: I tested ML meta-labeling on my crypto trend bot and it added nothing (AUC 0.52). Is a plain 4h EMA system the better path? Looking for critique
author: Repulsive_Cloud_7435
selftext:
How I got here: a few weeks ago I saw a Twitter post with a "prompt to get rich with Claude." I didn't get rich, obviously, but I was surprised by how fast and how well the AI could build and test things with me. So I kept going: \~250 variants backtested, most of them failed, and what's left is the simple system below. Now I want humans to tell me what I'm missing.



Hobbyist here, small account (\~$240, money I can afford to lose). I tried adding machine learning as a filter on my rule-based trend bot (20 features, walk-forward, 3 models). AUC came out at 0.51–0.53 and it didn't beat random filtering, so I'm running the plain rules live. I'd like experienced eyes on the method before I trust it.



**Rules (fixed in advance, not optimized):**



\- 45 altcoin USDT-M perpetuals, 4h candles

\- Entry: EMA 20/50 cross, only in the direction of EMA 200. Limit order 0.05% better than the close, valid 60 min (skipped if not filled)

\- Exit: initial stop 2 ATR(14), trailing stop 3 ATR from the best price, 20-day max

\- Fixed $12.5 per trade (LONG at 64% of that), 3x, max 8 positions per side

https://i.redd.it/anur5xfb9w0i1.png

**Backtest (1h candles, taker 0.05% / maker 0.02% / slippage 0.055% / funding included):**



\- Nov 2020–Nov 2023: 1,285 trades, +$136, t ≈ 3.4, max drawdown $27

\- Nov 2023–Nov 2026: 1,705 trades, +$162, t ≈ 3.6, max drawdown $45

\- \~1/3 winners. The top 10% of winners make more than the total profit

\- 45 of 73 months positive. Worst month −$21.6

\- All 14 neighbor parameter sets (MA lengths, filters, stops, 2h/6h candles) were positive



**Tested and rejected:** BTC regime filters (ADX, trend), funding/OI/taker-ratio filters, fear & greed, ML meta-labeling (AUC 0.51–0.53), Donchian, pairs, grid, DCA, break-even stops, tighter trailing, top-100 universe, shorter timeframes. Most "improvements" just cut trades, so the drawdown went down but the edge didn't change.



**What worries me:**



1. **Selection bias**. The edge shows up in these 45 coins but NOT in other coins of similar age (top-100 universe ≈ 0). I picked the 45 for liquidity, not results, but still.

2. **It's mostly SHORT**. Altcoins bled vs USDT in 2024–25. LONG is around 0. If the regime flips, what then?

3. The last \~9 months are weak.



**Live**: running since Nov 3 with fixed rules. The plan is to judge it at 300 trades (pre-set: stop if average < 0, emergency stop at 100 trades if far worse than backtest). I size up to $18 only after 60 trades with execution matching paper.



**Questions**:



1. How would you test whether the 45-coin edge is real and not selection bias?

2. How do you handle a trend system whose edge depends on one side (SHORT) and one regime?

3. Does continuous sizing by trend strength (Carver style) make sense with such small size and exchange minimums?

4. Anything obviously wrong in how I'm measuring?

5. Has anyone gotten ML to add real value on top of a simple trend signal in crypto? What features or setup made the difference?



Thanks. Happy to share more numbers.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the 0.52 doesn't surprise me. you said the top 10% of winners make more than the whole total, so the system lives on a handful of trades nobody can tell apart from the losers at entry. a filter has to drop trades, and if it drops even two of the big ones it does damage. random filtering matching it is about what I'd expect.

what I'd check before trusting the plain rules is the entry. a limit 0.05% better than the close, good for 60 minutes, only fills when price comes back to you. the moves that run straight away from the cross never fill, and those are the candidates for your top 10%. on 1h candles the backtest can't really tell whether the limit was filled or only touched. run it once with market entries at the next open and see how much of the result is left.

also the 45 coins. if that's today's list applied back to 2020, every alt that died in between is missing, and you can't know which way that moves the result until they're in.
